name: Ida
label: Simple Machines
lede: Two voices, a four-track and a hardcore veteran's turn toward silence: Ida spent the 1990s making the quietest records on Simple Machines.

eras.title: Two voices and a four-track
eras.text: Daniel Littleton walked out of Annapolis hardcore and into a room with Elizabeth Mitchell, a guitar and a cassette recorder. What came out was hushed, homemade and nothing like what he had played before.

years.h: Ida starts as a duo: Daniel Littleton and Elizabeth Mitchell
years.p: [[Daniel Littleton|54a0c6a1-08bc-464d-be5d-1f571ad932e7]], who had fronted the Annapolis hardcore band [[The Hated|44a38273-7da3-433e-8213-554452f6f9bd]], begins writing and performing with [[Elizabeth Mitchell|03845f1b-b6bd-426a-b163-04b347e45270]]. The early recordings are quiet, lo-fi tapes.
years.xp:
Littleton grew up in Annapolis, Maryland, and sang in The Hated in the 1980s. Ida was a sharp turn: two voices, acoustic guitars and a lot of space between the notes.

Sources differ slightly on when the pair met (1990 in a Chronogram profile, 1991 on Wikipedia and in Littleton's podcast interview).

years.h: First show outside New York: a benefit in Washington, DC
years.p: Ida plays its first out-of-town date as a benefit concert in the capital, close to the punk scene Littleton came from.

years.cap: Littleton and Mitchell in the early Ida years
years.h: A demo tape lands with Jenny Toomey
years.p: After shows with double-bassist Rick Lassiter, the band records a 4-track cassette. [[Jenny Toomey|246fc8dd-a667-4a5b-868a-a5897bcd6c59]] of Simple Machines hears it and offers to put out an album.
years.xp: Simple Machines was the Arlington, Virginia label run by Toomey and Kristin Thomson, best known for its DIY tour manuals and bands like [[Tsunami|fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2]] and [[Circus Lupus|01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103]]. Toomey also made the electro-pop record Listening Cap with Littleton as Liquorice (4AD, 1995).

eras.title: Simple Machines and the sound of small rooms
eras.text: Three albums and a run of seven-inches for the Arlington label made Ida the gentlest band in the catalog. By I Know About You, critics were reaching for words like hushed and perfect.

years.h: Backing Lisa Loeb on "Stay (I Missed You)"
years.p: Mitchell and Littleton play behind [[Lisa Loeb|22c5cef9-80e8-48d2-acd3-6d16f6c8a16d]] on the song that lands on the Reality Bites soundtrack and becomes a number-one hit.

years.h: Tales of Brave Ida, the Simple Machines debut
years.p: Recorded largely as a duo, then fleshed out live when Littleton's brother Michael "Miggy" joins on drums.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the album to 1994; a Chronogram profile says 1995. Michael Littleton became the band's drummer and multi-instrumentalist soon after, and stayed until 1999.

years.h: I Know About You: the record fans still name first
years.p: Strings, upright bass and two voices blended so closely that the Chicago Tribune called them the prettiest in the land. Alternative Press gave it five stars.
years.xp:
The album features viola and violin from Cecilia Littleton Bonner and upright bass and string arrangements from Rick Lassiter. "When I Was Now" is a cover of a Cindy Kallet song, not an Ida original.

The Village Voice called it the best Ida album, and Pitchfork later reviewed it with high praise.

years.h: Karla Schickele joins on bass and vocals
years.p: [[Karla Schickele|cd341b7e-2628-49ee-8138-6177c96a0e9f]], daughter of composer [[Peter Schickele|8d748f6a-e24c-49cf-b93a-93e9d2fa48b3]] and leader of Beekeeper, becomes a permanent member and stays for the rest of the band's run.
years.xp: Wikipedia says she joined in late 1996; Chronogram says 1997. She went on to record solo as k and co-founded the Willie Mae Rock and Roll Camp for Girls in Brooklyn.

years.h: Ten Small Paces closes the Simple Machines run
years.p: The third and last Ida album for the label, with Schickele now in the line-up.

eras.title: Chamber pop, Capitol and a marriage
eras.text: Violins, cello and clarinet joined the folk core, and Ida got labelled chamber pop. A major label came and went, and the record everyone remembers came out on Tiger Style.

years.h: Two EPs: Losing True and The Ida Retsin Family
years.p: Between albums, Ida puts out two EPs while touring with classical players, among them violinist Ida Pearle, cellist Elaine Ahn and clarinetist Sue Havens.

years.h: Michael Littleton leaves; Mitchell and Littleton marry
years.p: Drummer [[Michael Littleton|c24f60a1-3cc1-4e22-bcc2-d38d9b105d87]] departs and goes on to White Magic and [[Blood on the Wall|8e4c8cc7-b5af-4329-a7ca-3d92c3a9ddb7]]. His brother and Mitchell marry the same year.

years.big: A major label, three albums of tapes, no release
years.h: Capitol Records signs Ida, then lets go
years.p: Ida signs to Capitol, records material for about three albums, then leaves after the label restructures. The band keeps ownership of the masters.
years.xp: According to a Strand Magazine interview with Littleton, the Capitol-era recordings stayed with the band after the exit. The songs were reworked for later records.

years.h: Will You Find Me on Tiger Style makes the year-end lists
years.p: Spin and The New York Times both name it a best-of-the-year record; The New Yorker and Village Voice praise it too.
years.xp: Numero Group later reissued the album as a four-LP set, the reason Ida returned to the stage in 2023.

years.cap: Will You Find Me, Tiger Style, 2000
years.h: The album that made Ida's name outside the indie world
years.p: Ida's fullest arrangements yet, with strings and a wider band around Littleton, Mitchell and Schickele.

years.h: The Braille Night follows Will You Find Me
years.p: The upright bass of Zach Mitchell and the violin of Ida Pearle join the line-up around the record.

years.h: Daughter Storey is born; the band slows down
years.p: Storey Littleton is born to Mitchell and Littleton. The family leaves Brooklyn for Providence, then Woodstock, and Ida goes quiet for a stretch.

eras.title: Woodstock and Levon's barn
eras.text: Ida moved up the Hudson and made its most rooted records. Mitchell became a children's-music star on the side, and the band ended without a fight in 2010.

years.h: Move to Woodstock, New York
years.p: After Brooklyn and Providence, Mitchell and Littleton settle in the Hudson Valley for good.

years.h: Heart Like a River on Polyvinyl
years.p: A quieter, pastoral record. Violinist Jean Cook and then drummer Ruth Keating join the band.
years.xp: Littleton described the approach as more pastoral and stripped down, all about the space between the sounds.

years.h: Jean Cook and Ruth Keating join
years.p: [[Jean Cook|c304c9c2-e3f3-4abb-b7ca-61f86f4889f5]], who plays with the Mekons, and drummer Ruth Keating fill out the Woodstock-era Ida.

years.h: Lovers Prayers at Levon Helm's studio
years.p: Recorded at [[Levon Helm|392baa89-ea47-4de6-8dc0-fdac3ec85509]]'s barn in Woodstock, with Helm and folk singer [[Michael Hurley|a45bbcf5-f009-49cb-962e-4591083573d1]] appearing on the record.

years.h: On NPR's Bryant Park Project
years.p: Ida performs on the show; its songs also turn up on This American Life.

years.h: Ida Con Snock with Michael Hurley
years.p: A collaboration with the folk eccentric on Gnomonsong, plus the EP My Fair, My Dark.

years.h: Ida disbands after a decade of records
years.p: Mitchell continues as a children's-music artist on Smithsonian Folkways; Littleton turns to free improvisation projects.

eras.title: Back on stage
eras.text: A reissue of Will You Find Me pulled the band out of retirement and onto a tour with its old Simple Machines labelmates.

years.h: Reunion at the Numero Twenty show in Los Angeles
years.p: Ida plays for the first time in over a decade at the Numero Group's anniversary show, tied to its four-LP reissue of Will You Find Me.

years.h: Co-headlining tour with Tsunami
years.p: Ida and fellow Simple Machines band [[Tsunami|fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2]] swap opener and headliner slots each night on a national tour.

sources.title: Strand Magazine: interview with Daniel Littleton
